who: Historian of the British Empire and South Africa, McGill University.

evidence.says: The department magazine lists Elizabeth Elbourne and Jason Opal as supervisors of Stephan Robert Pigeon’s Scissors-and-Paste dissertation, matching the listed student and title.
The candidate’s public ORCID employment record identifies Elizabeth Elbourne as Associate Professor in McGill’s Department of History and Classical Studies.
The alternative candidate’s LC authority identifies Elizabeth Elbourne as the author of Blood Ground (2002).
McGill’s institutional publication list attributes Blood Ground (2002) to Elizabeth Elbourne.

notes: Selected the ORCID-bearing p-9564. The LC-bearing p-2088 also matches through Blood Ground; the candidates appear to duplicate the same historian.

who: Philip Alden Kuhn, historian of China, Harvard faculty from 1978; Harvard PhD in History and East Asian Languages.

evidence.says: Harvard identifies Philip A. Kuhn as its professor of History and East Asian Languages and Civilizations from 1978, after teaching at Chicago, and describes his Harvard doctorate and Chinese-history scholarship.
The candidate’s LC authority identifies Philip A. Kuhn as a Harvard history professor and records the name Philip Alden Kuhn.

notes: Institution, period and Chinese-history field agree. The alternative ORCID candidate p-21506 supplies only a name and no public employment evidence establishing this identity.

who: David William Miller, historian of Ireland, Carnegie Mellon faculty from 1967; PhD Chicago 1968.

evidence.says: CMU identifies David William Miller as its history professor from 1967 and names Peter Gilmore, Cian McMahon and Jay Roszman among his graduate students, matching three listed students.
The candidate’s LC authority identifies David William/David W. Miller as a Carnegie Mellon historian of Ireland, faculty 1967–2012, with a Chicago history doctorate in 1968.

notes: The supplied candidate name omits W.; its LC identifier establishes the full identity. The alternative David B. Miller authority concerns the author of Rapid City, Gateway to the Hills.

who: E. Randolph (Emmett Randolph) Daniel, medieval historian at the University of Kentucky; PhD Virginia 1966.

evidence.says: LC explicitly records E. Randolph/Emmett Randolph Daniel as a medieval historian at Kentucky with a University of Virginia PhD in 1966; a 1983 source identifies him as Kentucky professor of history.
Kentucky’s 2006 department newsletter lists Randolph Daniel as Professor Emeritus and describes his work on Angelo Clareno.

notes: The LC candidate matches the exact doctoral institution and year as well as the students’ department and medieval field.

who: James Zachary Rabun, historian at Emory University; PhD Chicago 1948 according to Emory’s catalogue.

evidence.says: George R. Lamplugh’s own CV names James Z. Rabun as director of Politics on the Periphery, Emory PhD 1973, exactly matching the listed dissertation.
Emory lists James Z. Rabun as Professor of History with a University of Chicago PhD in 1948.
LC identifies James Z. (James Zachary) Rabun as an Emory University history professor.

notes: Direct student testimony and the exact doctorate match identify the James Zachary candidate.

who: Manuel P. Servín, historian of Mexico and Latin America at USC and Arizona State; PhD USC 1959.

evidence.says: LC records Manuel P. Servín’s USC PhD in 1959, subsequent teaching at USC, and move to Arizona State in the early 1970s to teach Mexican American history.
A February 13, 1967 governor’s press release preserved by NARA identifies Manuel P. Servin as USC associate professor and Latin American Studies co-director, with a USC history PhD in 1959.

notes: Both teaching institutions and the exact doctorate agree. The alternative LC n98047057 identifies an optics researcher, author of Interferogram Analysis for Optical Testing.

who: James Patrick Shenton, historian of the United States at Columbia, faculty 1951–1996; PhD Columbia 1954.

evidence.says: Columbia identifies James Patrick Shenton as an American historian, gives his Columbia PhD in 1954 and faculty service from 1951 to 1996.
LC identifies James P. Shenton as James Patrick Shenton, Columbia University history professor.

notes: Full name, department, period and exact doctoral institution/year agree.

who: Guy Salvatore Alitto, historian of modern China at the University of Chicago; PhD Harvard 1975.

evidence.says: Chicago’s History Department identifies Guy Salvatore Alitto as emeritus associate professor of History and East Asian Languages and Civilizations, with a Harvard PhD in 1975 and graduate teaching in modern Chinese history.
LC records Guy Alitto/Guy S. Alitto as a University of Chicago professor, citing the university’s East Asian Library and a 1986 publication.

notes: The candidate’s institution and Chinese-history field agree with the students, and Harvard agrees with the AHA’s own-PhD entry.
